build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The plane moves with physics-based momentum: thrust accelerates, gravity pulls down, and turning has inertia. The player must manage energy state (speed vs altitude). Score 0 if movement is instant or grid-based with no physics.
The plane fires weapons in its facing direction, with projectiles that travel ballistically and destroy enemies on hit with visible feedback. Score 0 if the plane cannot fire or hits have no effect.
Score milestones unlock new plane parts that can be equipped in a hangar screen, visibly changing the plane's appearance and performance. Score 0 if no unlock or customization system exists.
A hangar or loadout screen allows equipping different parts (engine, wings, weapons) onto the plane with visible stat changes and weight/energy constraints. Score 0 if no customization screen exists.

The plane has a health or damage system with visible damage states, and destruction triggers a crash animation and sortie failure. Score 0 if the plane is invincible or destruction has no consequence.
At least 6 sorties or missions with different sky environments, enemy compositions, and objectives. Score 0 if only one mission exists.
At least 4 distinct enemy aircraft types with different flight behaviors (dive bombers, circling aces, heavy gunships, fast interceptors). Score 0 if only one enemy type exists.
At least 4 customizable part categories (engine, wings, weapons, armor) with multiple options per category offering meaningful tradeoffs. Score 0 if no parts exist.
Boss encounters feature large aircraft with multiple turrets, distinct attack phases, and weak points that must be targeted. Score 0 if no bosses exist.
A sortie debrief screen shows score, enemies destroyed, accuracy, damage taken, and any new unlocks earned. Score 0 if missions end abruptly with no summary.

Normal startup shows a styled hangar or title screen with the plane displayed, a sortie-select control, and aviation-themed imagery. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The flow connects hangar to sortie selection to aerial combat to debrief without restarting the executable. Score 0 if major transitions are missing.
The HUD clearly shows speed/altitude indicators, health, ammo, score, and objective status in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot determine flight state.

Player actions produce visible feedback: thrust shows exhaust, hits show sparks, enemy destruction shows explosions, damage shows smoke trails, and stalls show warning indicators. Score 0 if actions happen silently.

Art direction is coherent across hangar, sky environments, aircraft, HUD, and menus with a consistent aviation palette and style. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
The player plane, enemy aircraft, projectiles, clouds, and environmental elements use real sprite art with distinct designs. Score 0 if primary gameplay elements are unstyled rectangles.
Animation brings the sky to life: plane banking animations, exhaust trails, cloud parallax, explosion sequences, and damage smoke effects. Score 0 if all elements are static.
HUD and UI panels use styled themed widgets with aviation instruments, framed panels, or custom fonts rather than raw HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all UI is default Label/Button.
